findings.text: Every program's gate: the request names each step's holder, only that person records it (or it says recorded as them), Approve waits on open items, and deliverables never flip.
PDR's Interconnections deliverable reads the agreements: Not ready, 2 expired · 2 unsigned, and opens Interconnections showing just those four.
A decision records only the decision: deliverables and criteria keep reading their records, so PDR stays 2 of 5 ready and 2 of 4 met after it passes.
The ATO condition's progress, ConMon's trigger and the package's POA&M count read the live issue and POA&M registers (lane F's facts) at draw time.
Increment 1's IATT is one record: Nov 18, 2025, ATD Aug 31, 2026, the developmental test article, read by Lifecycle and Authorization.
Beside Submit for review the page says it needs a review comment, with a link to the field; with one, SSP 3 goes to the ISSM.
Approve is unavailable while a deliverable or criterion is open; with conditions and Not approved stay. A request far ahead, or with earlier steps open, says so.
Lifecycle's IATT and ATO steps write one authorization record; Authorization's decision history, Boundary's IATT and Block 1.1 views read it, including Increment 2's planned IATT.
With conditions the row reads Passed with conditions; each condition has an owner and due day on Lifecycle, the gate and its owner's My work until closed.
Each step of a chain is recorded on its own, naming the current holder (ISSM, then SCA, then AO), as risk acceptance does.
PDR's Boundary opens a Block 1.1 view with the SCA's boundary review shown, requestable and recordable; recording it makes the deliverable ready.
Each security outcome has one status per increment, read by every gate and the outcomes view: RM.3 reads Not assessed on both the strategy and Milestone B.
Develop the SSP reads In progress, its deliverable SSP revision 3 In progress · draft, 74 placeholder narratives, then the review's state.
Package version 2 holds revision 2.1, Increment 1's annual update, with its own review; SSP revision 3 feeds Increment 2's CDR and IATT.
findings.why: ConMon's significant-change trigger (lane W) and Plan an assessment's SSP choice (Assessments) still name SSP 3 and SSP 2.

findings.text: The SAR step's first step records the SCA's risk recommendation and residual risk; the package shows it. Authorization records read ATO, ATO with conditions, IATT, DATO.
Requirements · 14 controls with no requirement opens the SCTM workbook's No requirement view: exactly the 14 controls.
findings.why: Controls (lane F's page) has no No requirement quick view to open; asked.

findings.text: The AO, or the AODR when chosen, decides Select security controls and Develop the SSP; the SCA's step reviews.
SSP 3's review reads the categorization rationale from ITCSC version 3, signed Sep 2, so nothing blocks submission.
findings.why: The SSP editor's section 2 (route ssp, not lane G's) still draws the rationale empty.

findings.text: The outcomes view uses Lifecycle's status words and drops the stale footnote; My work's Waiting on others lists the decisions the reader requested.
Lifecycle owns each gate's criteria, deliverables and decision; Security engineering becomes Lifecycle's Security outcomes view reading the same statuses.
Authorization's decision history reads Increment 1's IATT from Lifecycle (Nov 18, 2025) and lists Increment 2's, due May 18, 2027.
Package room becomes Authorization's Sharing tab (recipients, access requests, access log); Authorization alone holds versions, readiness and the decision.

extra.text: Request decision is offered on any undecided step, not only the next one, with the warning saying what is early or open.
The line under the program switcher and My work's Due for group count the next gate's deliverables as Lifecycle does.
Increment 1's three ATO conditions have owners and due days; one counts open high issues, one closes itself when the increment 2 results publish.
A signed memo and the authorization decision are listed as the decision's own records, not inputs, so they never block or fake readiness.
